oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Alert — embeddings-service-prod (west1) showing surge in 5xxs and tail latency. First seen 22:14 UTC. Pager triggered. Incident INC-2026-314.
Aisha: I'm taking initial ownership for the next 10m while I finish the evening handoff. Quick status: # of 5xxs spiked ~120rps, error is `grpc: connection reset by peer` from model-host pods, increased request queue depth on the batched worker.
Diego: On my way in — ETA 4min. If you need me to take driver during the shift swap I'm happy to. Any immediate mitigation I should run before I hop in?
Aisha: Yes please take driver if you can. I'll stay as secondary (observability + context) and hand comms to Kira. Action plan: 1) Reduce client concurrency to drain queues; 2) Restart model-host pods with new env to disable large-batch optimization temporarily; 3) If errors persist, failover to model-quantized-v2.
Kira: I'll be comms owner for the handoff. Notifying accounts that might be affected (support + account-ops). Aisha, can you paste the runbook pointer and the `kubectl` checks?
Aisha: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-p1 (see "shift-handovers" section). Quick checks: ```
# tail request queues across nodes
kubectl -n inference exec -it deployment/embeddings-queue -- curl localhost:9000/queues

# view recent model-host errors
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-host -c host --since=10m | grep -i "connection reset" | tail -n 100

# scale down client concurrency (temporary)
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/embeddings-client MAX_CONCURRENCY=8
```
Diego: Got it. I'm jumping in as driver now. I'll perform the checks and start with reducing MAX_CONCURRENCY, then rolling restarts of the model-host pods one AZ at a time. Kira, once I confirm reduced error rate I'll ask you to notify support to pause outbound escalations.
Sam: Quick suggestion from SRE side: before full restarts, try toggling `BATCH_OPTIMIZER=false` on one model-host to verify behavior (can limit blast radius). If that stabilizes, we can propagate to others. Also watch GPU mem VS locked pages.
Aisha: Good call. Diego, please try Sam's test on one pod first. After you switch, monitor 95/99th tail latency and 5xx counts for 2 mins. If errors drop >= 70% and latency stays within 2x baseline, proceed to roll.
Diego: Doing toggle on pod model-host-7 now. Command I ran: ```
kubectl -n inference exec model-host-7 -- sh -c "export BATCH_OPTIMIZER=false && supervisorctl restart model-host"
``` Will report in ~90s.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Handoff recorded — driver: Diego, comms: Kira, secondary: Aisha. Incident INC-2026-314.
Diego: After 90s: error rate dropped ~78%, tail latency up 1.4x but p95 ok. Rolling restart of remaining model-host pods in progress (one AZ at a time). Monitoring metrics: dashboard link https://kibana.redwood.internal/d/embeds/prod-overview?from=-15m
Kira: Contacted support with a short note and affected customers list. Holding public comms until you confirm stable for 10m. Posting summary in #customer-impact if we cross that threshold.
Aisha: Noted. Leaving the bridge to Diego and Kira. I'm switching my Slack status to "handoff-complete" and will catch follow-ups tomorrow morning. Good handover. :thumbsup:
Diego: Acknowledged. I'll mark ownership in PagerDuty and escalate if we see regression. If anything changes please ping `@oncall-bot` with `handoff:update`.
Sam: I'll keep an eye on infra metrics; if rolling restart looks noisy I'll be ready to scale up an extra worker pool (reserved capacity) as contingency.
Kira: All set from comms. I'll draft a brief incident status after 10m stable window.
Aisha: Thanks team — handoff complete.
